observations: Newton–Euler uses linkwise free-body force/torque balances and recursive calculation. Lagrangian modelling uses scalar energies and independent coordinates, eliminating ideal constraint reactions already incorporated by those coordinates.

Model-based control and AI-driven dynamics learning are stated applications, not guarantees of fitted parameters, complete loads or validated predictions.

observations: Translational kinetic energy is one-half mass times speed squared; fixed-axis rotational energy is one-half inertia times squared angular speed.
Net work changes kinetic energy: accelerating from rest adds energy, whereas stopping entails negative work on the body and positive mechanical energy removed.

pages.inspectionBasis: Initial source-first inspection before keyed access; targeted revision/gap source pages reinspected at 17:32 UTC.
observations: The massless single arm has a tip mass, a zero-angle undeflected torsional spring, rightward X and downward Y; theta is downward-positive.
Tip downward coordinate is l sin(theta), so gravitational U is negative with downward displacement. Spring energy is one-half kt theta squared and physical restoring torque is −kt theta.
K is one-half m l squared times angular rate squared. Energy and power consequences require the stated undamped assumptions.
